grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; no grading rule imposes a deduction.
grade.summary: The submission gives a complete and correct proof. The lexicographic potential (product, number of entries greater than 1) proves termination, and the argument that a move cannot eliminate the last two nonunit entries proves the terminal board has exactly one entry greater than 1. Primewise, the move applies the Euclidean-algorithm transformation (a,b) to (min(a,b),|a-b|), preserving the gcd of all p-adic valuations. At a terminal board this invariant equals v_p(M), determining M uniquely from the initial board.
strengths: Correctly computes that the board product is divided by gcd(m,n) at each move.
Uses a valid well-founded lexicographic potential to prove finite termination.
Correctly establishes that the terminal number of entries greater than 1 is exactly one.
Identifies and proves the relevant primewise valuation invariant.
Correctly reconstructs the unique terminal value as the product of p raised to the gcd of the initial p-adic valuations.
Verifies that this reconstructed value is greater than 1.
